1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that vide notification bearing No.
F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, the Government intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".

4. It is stated that the petitioner is the interested person and is owner/bhumidhar in actual and physical possession of 1/4th share of the land bearing Khasra no. 38/10 (800), 11 (610), 20 (6 07), 40/22/2 min (3 12), total 24 Bigha 9 biswa (in short the said land) situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi.
5. It is stated that the petitioner is entitled to receive the compensation amount of the actual prevailing market value of the said land.
The actual physical possession of the said land is with the petitioner as the physical possession of the land has not been taken and the respondents shall take possession thereof from the petitioner.

The LAC passed the award in a mechanical way without applying the mind and without going through the claim filed by the petitioner, as such the award is not acceptable to the petitioner, and he is receiving the awarded amount under protest and without prejudice to their rights.

The LAC failed to take note of the actual LAC no. 399/2016 (Award No.
08/200506/DC(NW)) Sarup Singh v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 and practical market value and had adopted a narrow approach while observing that no proof of claim market value is attached.

status, potentiality and development of the said land and its surroundings.

The ld. Counsel for the petitioner has taken the following grounds :
(i) It is stated that the holdings of the petitioner is well connected with the transport,
telecommunication, roads and have all the basic amenities in and around the surrounding areas i.e. NH10, Delhi Rohtak Road and the said land is near the Main Karala Mundka Road and the said land is situated by many prestigious colonies/village/industries area and the value of each and every commodity has been raised day by day.
(ii) The said land has potential value as the said land is sorrounded by villages like Mundka, Ghevra, Kanjhawala, Nangloi, Karala, mubarakpur and the value in the abovesaid area is not less than Rs. 5,000/ per square yards.

The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

8. It is submitted that the compensation award by the LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

9. It is stated that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days, therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
14. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.
My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLE TO THE ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF SO, TO WHAT EXTENT ? OPP 15.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
LAC no. 399/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Sarup Singh v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 12 16.

During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.

Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
17.
Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

18. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

19. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre Sh. Sarup Singh vs Union Of India on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180496153/
5 i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.

The petitioners are, accordingly LAC no. 399/2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Sarup Singh v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 12 entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).

20 . The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
RELIEF 21.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioner is granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).

(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
